question: What constitutes the fishing and fisheries sector in Uganda and who are the key industry players?
answer: Uganda's fisheries sector encompasses capturing, handling, processing, and trading fish across freshwater lakes (Lake Victoria, Lake Albert, Lake Kyoga, Lake Edward, Lake George) and river basins, along with commercial aquaculture. The sector is structured into four main operational categories: 1) Fishermen — individuals who catch or harvest fish using authorized canoes and fishing vessels; 2) Fishmongers — wholesale and retail traders who purchase fresh catch at landing sites and distribute to domestic markets and urban centers; 3) Fish Processors — industrial plants that gut, fillet, freeze, smoke, or can fish for institutional buyers and premium commercial markets; 4) Fish Exporters — commercial entities licensed to export chilled Nile perch fillets, frozen tilapia, smoked fish, and fish maws (swim bladders) to regional and international markets.

question: What government licenses and registrations are required to operate a fishing, fishmonger, processing, or exporting business in Uganda?
answer: Operators in the fisheries value chain must comply with multi-agency licensing: 1) Business Registration: Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) for business names or company incorporation; 2) Sector Licensing: Directorate of Fisheries Resources (DFR) under the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF) for commercial fishing vessel licenses, fish movement permits, and fish health/sanitary certificates; 3) Local Landing Site Permits: District local governments and landing site Beach Management Units (BMUs) for landing and trading authorization; 4) Quality Standards: Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) certification for fish processing factories; 5) Tax Registration: Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) 10-digit TIN with obligations for Corporation Tax (or Presumptive Tax), PAYE, VAT, and Withholding Tax.

question: How does Value Added Tax (VAT) apply to fresh fish, processed fish, and exported fish products in Uganda?
answer: Under the Value Added Tax Act: 1) Fresh, Raw Fish: Unprocessed fresh fish, whole fish, and raw foodstuffs caught and landed by fishermen are strictly EXEMPT from VAT under Schedule 2 of the VAT Act (no VAT is charged); 2) Processed Fish: Fish that has undergone industrial value addition (filleting, deep freezing, packaging, salting, or canning) sold on the domestic market is a standard-rated supply attracting 18% VAT; fish processing plants must register for VAT and EFRIS to issue fiscal invoices; 3) Exported Fish: The export of fish products (chilled Nile perch, frozen fish, fish maws) outside Uganda is ZERO-RATED (0% VAT) under Schedule 3 of the VAT Act, enabling registered exporters to claim full input VAT refunds on operational inputs.

question: What income tax rules apply to small fishmongers versus commercial fish processing and exporting companies?
answer: 1) Small Fishmongers & Artisanal Fishermen: Resident sole proprietor fishmongers with annual gross sales between UGX 10,000,000 and UGX 150,000,000 pay simplified presumptive turnover tax (0.4%–0.7% with records or fixed lump-sum schedules without records); payment of presumptive tax serves as filing their annual return; turnover under UGX 10M pays Nil tax; 2) Industrial Fish Processors & Exporters: Incorporated fish processing and exporting firms pay standard thirty percent (30%) Corporation Income Tax (CIT) on net chargeable profits, submitting twice-yearly provisional returns via Form DT-1001; 3) 10-Year Income Tax Holiday: Under Section 21(1)(y) of the Income Tax Act, fish processors who invest in industrial parks or free zones and export at least 80% of their production outside the domestic tariff area enjoy a 10-year income tax holiday.

question: What customs duty and tax exemptions apply to fishing vessels, aquaculture inputs, and fish export packaging?
answer: Under the Fifth Schedule of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA 2004) Part B: 1) Fresh Catch Landed: Fish, crustaceans, and molluscs (fresh, chilled, or frozen) caught and landed by canoes or fishing vessels registered and based in an EAC Partner State are exempt from all import taxes; 2) Aquaculture Inputs: Fish eggs, fry, and fingerlings (young fish) imported for aquaculture fish farming are exempt from all customs duties and taxes; 3) Processing Machinery: Industrial dairy and food/fish processing machinery attracts 0% import duty under the EAC Common External Tariff (CET); 4) Export Packaging: Specialized packaging material of any kind designed for packaging fish for export is 100% exempt from import duty and taxes.
